title: Hypnosis in therapy - pain management for the body and mind, with David Patterson, PhD

sentences.en: What comes to mind when you think of hypnosis?
sentences.zh: 提到催眠，你会想到什么？

sentences.en: A swinging pocket watch?
sentences.zh: 是一块摇晃的怀表吗？

sentences.en: A hapless volunteer on a stage clucking like a chicken?
sentences.zh: 还是舞台上那个笨拙的志愿者像鸡一样咯咯叫？

sentences.en: Hypnosis, in many people's minds, is the province of charlatans and showmen.
sentences.zh: 在许多人心中，催眠是江湖骗子和表演者的领域。

sentences.en: But this image of hypnosis is outdated and misleading.
sentences.zh: 但这种催眠的形象已经过时且具有误导性。

sentences.en: Over the past several decades, psychologists and other researchers have learned more about how hypnosis actually works, and they found evidence that it can be useful in treating
sentences.zh: 在过去的几十年里，心理学家和其他研究人员对催眠的实际运作方式有了更多了解，他们发现有证据表明它在治疗方面很有用

sentences.en: pain, anxiety, and a range of other physical and mental health probleMs.
sentences.zh: 疼痛、焦虑以及一系列其他身心健康问题。

sentences.en: So what exactly is happening in people's bodies and brains when they're hypnotized?
sentences.zh: 那么，当人们被催眠时，他们的身体和大脑到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: What's the difference between stage tricks and hypnotherapy used in pain management?
sentences.zh: 舞台戏法与用于疼痛管理的催眠疗法之间有什么区别？

sentences.en: Can anyone be hypnotized?
sentences.zh: 任何人都能被催眠吗？

sentences.en: What kinds of physical and mental health issues can hypnosis address?
sentences.zh: 催眠可以解决哪些身心健康问题？

sentences.en: And if you want to see whether hypnosis can help you, how can you find a qualified practitioner whom you can trust?
sentences.zh: 如果你想看看催眠是否能帮助你，该如何找到一位值得信赖的合格从业者？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》，这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: My guest today is Dr. David Patterson, a professor of medicine and psychology at the University of
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是戴维·帕特森博士，他是华盛顿大学医学院的医学和心理学教授。

sentences.en: Washington School of Medicine.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿大学医学院。

sentences.en: Dr. Patterson specializes in pain control and recovery from physical trauma, burn injuries, and other forms of disabilities.
sentences.zh: 帕特森博士专门研究疼痛控制以及身体创伤、烧伤和其他形式残疾的康复。

sentences.en: He is also internationally known for his work in clinical hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 他在临床催眠领域也享誉国际。

sentences.en: Over the past several decades, he has led many National Institutes of Health-funded studies
sentences.zh: 在过去的几十年里，他领导了许多由美国国立卫生研究院资助的研究，

sentences.en: on hypnosis for pain management, has published more than 100 articles on hypnosis in peer-reviewed journals, and has written a book for APA on hypnosis for pain control.
sentences.zh: 研究内容涉及疼痛管理的催眠，在同行评审期刊上发表了100多篇关于催眠的文章，并为美国心理学会撰写了一本关于疼痛控制催眠的书。

sentences.en: Dr. Patterson, thank you for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 帕特森博士，感谢您今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you, Kim.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。

sentences.en: It's an honor to be here, and I wanted to thank you.
sentences.zh: 能来到这里是我的荣幸，我也想谢谢你。

sentences.en: It's my understanding that you've started this podcast, and I've listened to several of them,
sentences.zh: 据我了解，你创办了这个播客，我也听过其中的几期，

sentences.en: and it's a wonderful way to take popular topics and really provide a scientific basis that psychology can provide.
sentences.zh: 这是一种将热门话题与心理学所能提供的科学基础相结合的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: So my compliments and appreciation to you.
sentences.zh: 所以我向你表示赞赏和感谢。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 好的，谢谢。

sentences.en: And I think we're going to do that today because we will demystify hypnosis, I hope, and explain it scientifically.
sentences.zh: 我想我们今天会做到这一点，因为我希望我们能揭开催眠的神秘面纱，并从科学角度进行解释。

sentences.en: So let's start with that image problem I alluded to in the introduction.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从我在引言中提到的那个形象问题开始吧。

sentences.en: What is the difference between the hypnosis that you and other psychologists practice and the kind of stage tricks that may come to mind when some people think about hypnosis?
sentences.zh: 你和其他心理学家所实践的催眠，与某些人在想到催眠时可能想到的舞台戏法之间，有什么区别？

sentences.en: I'll start with stage hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 我先从舞台催眠说起。

sentences.en: And that, you know, most people have a concept of hypnosis based on what they've seen on TV.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大多数人对催眠的概念是基于他们在电视上看到的内容。

sentences.en: And interesting little trick about stage hypnosis, if you watch a lot of them work, what they will do is get 20 volunteers up on stage.
sentences.zh: 关于舞台催眠有一个有趣的小把戏，如果你观察过很多人的表演，你会发现他们会找20名志愿者上台。

sentences.en: They'll give them a suggestion, and they'll see that maybe five of them will really follow the suggestion deeply, like falling asleep on their neighbor's shoulder or whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们会给出一个暗示，然后你会看到可能其中五个人会非常深入地遵循这个暗示，比如靠在邻居的肩膀上睡着之类的。

sentences.en: So they send the rest of the people back to their seats, and they work with those highly hypnotizable people, and they make them do ridiculous things.
sentences.zh: 于是他们让其余的人回到座位上，只与那些高度易受催眠的人合作，让他们做一些荒谬的事情。

sentences.en: So one thing is that they select for hypnotizability, and the other is we're at the international
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，他们是挑选了易受催眠的人，另一方面，我们是在国际临床实验催眠学会的会议上。

sentences.en: meeting for International Society for Clinical Experimental Hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 我们请了一些来自拉斯维加斯的舞台催眠师与我们交谈，他们基本上强调的是人们想要参与到表演中来。

sentences.en: And we had some stage hypnotists from Las Vegas talk to us, and basically what they emphasized is people want to be part of the act.
sentences.zh: 所以催眠师也不确定他们是否真的被催眠了，但这已经成为了表演的一部分。

sentences.en: And so the hypnotists are not sure whether they're hypnotized or not, but it becomes kind of all part of the show.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 这就是舞台催眠。

sentences.en: So that's stage hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 作为心理学家，我们首先发现它远不止是安慰剂效应，

sentences.en: What we found as psychologists is, first of all, that it's far more than a placebo and
sentences.zh: 而且它可能是一种非常强大的治疗方法，你知道，你提到了疼痛和焦虑，肠易激综合征也是其中之一。

sentences.en: that it can be a very powerful treatment to, you know, you mentioned pain and anxiety, irritable bowel syndrome is another one.
sentences.zh: 但我们进行催眠的方式是，我们经常在研究人们时观察他们大脑中发生的事情，我们也会使用结果衡量标准。

sentences.en: But the way we do it is, I mean, we're very often looking at what's happening in the brain while we're studying people, and we're also using outcome measures.
sentences.zh: 我提到的最后一点，我认为非常重要，那就是众所周知，催眠可以大幅提高心理治疗的效果。

sentences.en: And the final thing I mentioned, and I think it's very important, is that hypnosis is known to increase the effect size of psychotherapy by a large amount.
sentences.zh: 那么，当人们被催眠时，他们的大脑和身体里发生了什么？

sentences.en: So what is happening in people's brains and bodies when they're hypnotized?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你把一个人放进功能性磁共振成像仪中进行催眠，他们的大脑会有什么不同的表现？

sentences.en: Like if you put somebody in an fMRI when they're hypnotized, how will their brains behave in a different way?
sentences.zh: 我听过谈论这个话题的人中，最好的一位叫皮埃尔·兰维尔，他在蒙特利尔。

sentences.en: One of the best people I've ever heard talk about this is named Pierre Rainville, and he's up in Montreal.
sentences.zh: 我曾经问过他，催眠时是否存在一种不同的大脑状态？

sentences.en: And I asked him once, is there a different brain state with hypnosis?
sentences.zh: 他说，你问错问题了，因为发生了一系列的大脑变化。

sentences.en: And he goes, you're asking the wrong question because there's a series of brain changes that happen.
sentences.zh: 所以你最初会看到左额叶的活动，因为人们在关注任何暗示。

sentences.en: So you initially see activity in a left frontal lobe as people attend to whatever the suggestions are.
sentences.zh: 这就是那块摇晃的怀表发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: And this is where the swinging watch comes in.
sentences.zh: 那只是吸引人们注意力的一种方式。

sentences.en: That's just a way to capture people's attention.
sentences.zh: 但随后发生的事情是，背外侧前额叶皮层似乎关闭了。

sentences.en: But then what happens is it looks like the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex shuts down.
sentences.zh: 所以额叶皮层的后部脱离了活动。

sentences.en: So the rear of the frontal cortex disengages.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，前扣带回（ACC），也就是我们大脑中激励我们的部分，参与了进来。

sentences.en: And then the ACC, which is the part of our brain that motivates us, engages us at the same time.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上发生的情况是，人们不再评判正在发生的事情，也不再关心正在发生的事情。

sentences.en: So basically what happens is that people give up judging what's happening to them or caring what's happening.
sentences.zh: 他们变得非常容易接受暗示。

sentences.en: And they just become very open to suggestion.
sentences.zh: 最后，当人们接受暗示时，你会看到大脑的不同部分被激活。

sentences.en: And then finally, as people get suggestions, you see different parts of the brain activated.
sentences.zh: 而且你经常会看到活动转移到非优势半球。

sentences.en: And very often you see a transfer of activity to the non-dominant hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 所以这确实是那三种现象：注意力增强、前额叶皮层抑制，以及根据暗示在大脑不同区域的参与。

sentences.en: So it's really those three phenomenon, increased attention, dampening of the prefrontal cortex, and then engagements in various areas of the brain depending on the suggestion.
sentences.zh: 而且它不是睡眠。

sentences.en: And it's not a sleep.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，人们是有意识的，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, people are conscious, right?
sentences.zh: 当他们处于这种状态时，他们知道周围发生了什么。

sentences.en: They know what's happening around them when they're in this state.
sentences.zh: 这是正确的吗？

sentences.en: Is that correct?
sentences.zh: 既是也不是。

sentences.en: Yes and no.
sentences.zh: 首先，我们喜欢消除对催眠的误解。

sentences.en: First of all, we like to dispel myths of hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 很多人害怕在催眠中睡着，但这几乎从未发生过，因为在某些文化中，这是一种尴尬的表现。

sentences.en: A lot of people are afraid to fall asleep with hypnosis, and that almost never happens because in some cultures, that's a form of embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 在大多数情况下，人们是意识到正在发生什么的。

sentences.en: And for the most part, people are aware of what's going on.
sentences.zh: 但在我们在心理治疗中使用的一些深度、复杂的催眠中，它通常就像是说你的大脑在浅睡眠中关闭了。

sentences.en: But with some of the deep, complex hypnosis that we use in psychotherapy, very often it's like saying your brain is shut off in a light sleep.
sentences.zh: 所以当人们处于这个阶段时，他们并没有睡着，但如果你告诉他们，我会打个响指，你就会醒来，他们会回应这个暗示。

sentences.en: So when people are in this phase, they're not asleep, but if you tell them that I'm going to snap my fingers and you'll wake up, they'll respond to the suggestion.
sentences.zh: 所以他们正在整合这些暗示，但有时他们的大脑会进入一种类似于暮色的功能状态。

sentences.en: So they're integrating the suggestions, but there are periods of time where it's just that their brain goes into a type of twilight form of functioning.
sentences.zh: 我们谈到了一些催眠可以解决的问题。

sentences.en: We talked a little bit about some of the problems that hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 我读过关于戒烟催眠的内容。

sentences.en: And I've read about hypnosis for smoking cessation.
sentences.zh: 我们提到了焦虑、失眠以及其他身心健康问题。

sentences.en: We mentioned anxiety, insomnia, other kinds of physical and mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 这些大多数都有研究支持吗？

sentences.en: Are most of these backed by research?
sentences.zh: 证据最强的是哪些方面？

sentences.en: And where is the evidence the strongest?
sentences.zh: 这些大多数确实有研究支持。

sentences.en: Most of these are indeed backed by research.
sentences.zh: 我认为最强有力的研究是在急性和慢性疼痛方面。

sentences.en: I think some of the strongest research is in acute and chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 特别是我的同事马克·詹森，他针对慢性疼痛进行了多次随机对照试验。

sentences.en: And particularly my colleague, Mark Jensen, has done a number of randomized controlled trials on chronic pain.
sentences.zh: 呃，我在烧伤疼痛和手术方面做了很多研究。

sentences.en: Uh, I, I did a lot on burn pain and surgeries.
sentences.zh: 肠易激综合征现在也有很多文献支持它。

sentences.en: There is irritable bowel syndrome has a lot of literature now, um, uh, to support it.
sentences.zh: 减轻焦虑，呃，戒烟。

sentences.en: Reduction of anxiety, uh, smoking sensation.
sentences.zh: 要找的名字是乔·格林。

sentences.en: And the name to look there is Joe Green.
sentences.zh: 他在这个领域做了很多工作。

sentences.en: He's done a lot of work on it.
sentences.zh: 呃，有一些证据表明催眠有助于减肥，不仅有帮助，而且使用催眠的人，减肥效果持续时间更长。

sentences.en: Uh, there is some evidence that hypnosis helps with, uh, weight loss, not only helps with it, but people who use hypnosis, the weight loss lasts longer.
sentences.zh: 呃，这些就是其中的一些例子。

sentences.en: Uh, and so those are, those are a few things.
sentences.zh: 我确实想再次强调，我认为使用催眠的最佳模式是让某人进行心理治疗，然后通过在适当的时候使用催眠来增强心理治疗的效果。

sentences.en: I do want to emphasize again, that I think the best model to use hypnosis is to have someone in psychotherapy and then basically boost the effects of psychotherapy therapy by using
sentences.zh: 所以，有些人是不是根本无法被催眠？

sentences.en: hypnosis at the right time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一个范围，对吧？

sentences.en: So are some people, they just can't be hypnotized at all.
sentences.zh: 关于谁能被催眠，谁不能被催眠。

sentences.en: I mean, there's like a range, right?
sentences.zh: 那条曲线看起来是什么样的？

sentences.en: Of who can be hypnotized and who can't be hypnotized.
sentences.zh: 是经典的钟形曲线吗？

sentences.en: Like what does that curve look like?
sentences.zh: 呃，你能从统计学上给我们一些概念吗，你知道，有多少，人口中能被催眠和不能被催眠的百分比是多少？

sentences.en: Is it a classic bell curve?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Uh, can you give us some idea of statistically, you know, how many, what's the percentage of the population that can be hypnotized and can't be hypnotized?
sentences.zh: 呃，首先，它确实是一个钟形曲线，就像你说的，可能有10%的人似乎根本没有反应，而在另一端有10%到15%的人非常容易受影响。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 它确实有点偏向于我们所说的轻度到中度易受催眠的人群。

sentences.en: Uh, first of all, it is a bell-shaped curve, like you said, and there's maybe, uh, 10% of people that just don't seem to respond and 10 to 15 people on the other tail that are
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人可能属于这一类。

sentences.en: very responsive.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，我们测量易受催眠性的方式是，你催眠某人，

sentences.en: It is a bit skewed to my, to what we would say mild to moderate hypnotizable.
sentences.zh: 你给他们一系列大约12个暗示，然后你的易受催眠性是通过他们遵循了多少个暗示来衡量的。

sentences.en: And so probably the majority of people fall in that category.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，这是一种循环论证，你知道，因为它实际上只是在说他们对多少个暗示有反应，而不是比这更特别的东西。

sentences.en: And just a quick note, the way, the way we measure it, hypnotize abilities, you hypnotize someone,
sentences.zh: 催眠不能做什么？

sentences.en: you give them a series of maybe 12 suggestions and you, you hypnotize ability is measured by how many suggestions they follow.
sentences.zh: 例如，一个高度易受暗示的人能否被催眠去谋杀或做一些他们在清醒、未被催眠的生活中不会做的事情？

sentences.en: And, uh, and, uh, and a sort of a circular argument, you know, because it's, it's really just saying
sentences.zh: 呃，很好的问题。

sentences.en: how many suggestions they respond to rather than something more special than that.
sentences.zh: 关于谋杀和反社会行为，答案是不，已经有许多研究证明了这一点。

sentences.en: What can hypnosis not do?
sentences.zh: 事实上，中央情报局，呃，我相信是在五十年代或六十年代，

sentences.en: For example, could somebody who is highly suggestible be hypnotized into committing murder or doing something that they wouldn't do in their waking non-hypnotized life?
sentences.zh: 追随“满洲候选人”的概念，试图催眠人们让他们成为杀手，或者是其他什么人。

sentences.en: Uh, excellent question.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，它从来没有真正奏效，所以人们不会做反社会行为。

sentences.en: And the first, the answer to committing murder and antisocial acts is no, there's been a number of studies that have demonstrated that.
sentences.zh: 呃，在大多数情况下，人们不会做他们不想做的事情。

sentences.en: And as a matter of fact, the CIA, uh, I believe this was in the fifties or sixties,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有那种“像鸡一样咯咯叫”的说法，但大多数人不会那样做，除非他们愿意配合表演。

sentences.en: followed the notion of the Manchurian man and try to hypnotize people to have them, uh, be hit men or hit women or, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 有没有人因为催眠可能弊大于利而不应该尝试？

sentences.en: And, uh, it, it never quite worked, but that, so people won't do antisocial acts.
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: Uh, and for the most part, people won't do what they don't want to do.
sentences.zh: 我认为，呃，我真的想提到那些在童年早期学会使用解离作为创伤反应的人群，呃，可能与性虐待有关，或者其他类型的创伤。

sentences.en: You know, there's the whole, uh, uh, cluck like a chicken and, but most people won't do that unless they're willing to go with the show.
sentences.zh: 他们使用它的频率如此之高，以至于它成为了他们人格的一部分。

sentences.en: Is there anyone who shouldn't try hypnosis because it could harm them more than help them?
sentences.zh: 这些人确实可以随时随地解离。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说他们永远不应该使用催眠，但当你对有严重解离倾向的人使用催眠时，你必须非常有条理，

sentences.en: And I think, uh, I want to really refer to groups of people who have learned to use dissociation
sentences.zh: 例如，不要让他们退行到童年早期，除非控制得非常好，因为那可能会引出许多破坏性的材料。

sentences.en: as a response to trauma early in their childhood, uh, perhaps with sexual abuse, um, or, or, or other types of trauma.
sentences.zh: 自我催眠怎么样？

sentences.en: And they, they use it so often that it becomes part of their personalities.
sentences.zh: 总是有很多关于如何自己学习催眠的讨论，你可以控制体重、戒烟或其他事情。

sentences.en: And these, these are people that can really dissociate with the drop of a hat.
sentences.zh: 这效果如何？

sentences.en: And I wouldn't say that they should never use hypnosis, but when you're using hypnosis with, uh, with people with really dissociative tendencies, you have to be very structured
sentences.zh: 它是否像被像你这样的科学从业者催眠一样有效？

sentences.en: and not, for example, not regress them to early childhood to, you know, unless it's very well controlled because that could bring up a lot of damaging material.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我认为我们用催眠所做的是，你实际上是在欺骗大脑的逻辑部分，让人们摆脱他们的认知自动功能。

sentences.en: What about self-hypnosis?
sentences.zh: 而且，有一种捕捉注意力的方法，有几种方法可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: He went in there.
sentences.zh: 他还是进去了。

sentences.en: He looked like he fell asleep.
sentences.zh: 看起来就像睡着了一样。

sentences.en: And we did all of his burn debridement.
sentences.zh: 然后我们完成了他所有的烧伤清创。

sentences.zh: 后来我做了一些工作，试图将沉浸式虚拟现实与催眠结合起来，作为一种传递催眠的载体。

sentences.en: And indeed there are two separate processes, you know, and, and, uh, we've published in journal of abnormal psychology on how you, you have these, uh, there's two separate

sentences.zh: 越来越少了。

sentences.en: And then I, I work hard to combine hypnosis with mindfulness, but hypnosis has had a waxing and white waning history since the 1800s.

sentences.en: And one of the reasons that kind of left the stage is, was the advent of ether.
sentences.zh: 它离开舞台的原因之一是乙醚的出现。

sentences.zh: 对病人使用乙醚要高效得多。

sentences.en: And there's, there definitely are, are changes in, in the way people process, uh, information when they're under hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 而且人们在催眠状态下处理信息的方式确实发生了变化。

sentences.en: Now, since the pandemic, a lot of therapy has moved online.
sentences.zh: 现在，自疫情以来，很多治疗都转移到了线上。

sentences.en: Is it possible to do hypnosis remotely?
sentences.zh: 远程进行催眠有可能吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对可以。

sentences.en: Uh, when I, uh, when the pandemic came along, you know, I'm,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当疫情来临时，你知道，我处于康复心理学和残疾领域，多年来我们一直呼吁为那些无法去诊所的人提供远程治疗。

sentences.en: I'm in the area of rehabilitation, psychology and disabilities and, and we've been screaming for remote treatment for years for people that can't get into the office.
sentences.zh: （接上句）多年来我们一直呼吁为那些无法去诊所的人提供远程治疗。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden pandemic comes along and in two weeks we're, we're set up with this whole platform.
sentences.zh: 然后疫情突然来袭，两周内我们就建立起了整个平台。

sentences.en: So I, uh, I was seeing all of my patients through, um, zoom and, uh, 90% of the hypnosis I did was over zoom.
sentences.zh: 所以我通过Zoom看我所有的病人，我做的90%的催眠都是通过Zoom进行的。

sentences.en: And again, what I would do is have the patients, uh, have their phone and, and record the session.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我会让病人拿着手机，录下治疗过程。

sentences.en: And then, but zoom's nice because it's not nearly as good as live hypnosis, but at least you can see, you know, see your patient.
sentences.zh: Zoom很好，虽然它远不如现场催眠好，但至少你可以看到你的病人。

sentences.en: And when you're with the patient and you're hypnotizing them, the ultimate scenario is that you're really in tune with their body, they're breathing
sentences.zh: 当你和病人在一起并催眠他们时，终极场景是你真正与他们的身体同步，他们的呼吸，你与他们一起呼吸。

sentences.en: and, and you're breathing with them.
sentences.zh: （接上句）你与他们一起呼吸。

sentences.en: And you, you notice that someone does, you know, just puts their head back and you reinforce that.
sentences.zh: 你会注意到有人把头向后仰，你就会强化这一点。

sentences.en: So there's a real advantage to being able to see the person much better in person than in zoom, but zoom works.
sentences.zh: 所以，面对面比通过Zoom能更好地观察到人确实有真正的优势，但Zoom也能行。

sentences.en: So I have to ask you another question related to some of these stage hypnotists.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须问你另一个关于那些舞台催眠师的问题。

sentences.en: Well, many, many years ago, I went to, uh, one of these sessions where a hypnotist was going to help people go through past life regression.
sentences.zh: 嗯，很多年前，我参加过一次这样的会议，一位催眠师要帮助人们进行前世回溯。

sentences.en: And in this demonstration, this person would hypnotize somebody who would then go back to what was supposed to be a prior life is, is this just quackery?
sentences.zh: 在这个演示中，这个人催眠了一个人，然后那个人回到了所谓的上一世，这只是江湖骗术吗？

sentences.en: I mean, what is going on when, when that happens?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当这种情况发生时，到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: And somebody comes along and says, well, I, I I'm in the foreSt. I know I'm a Navajo Indian.
sentences.zh: 有人走过来说，嗯，我在森林里。我知道我是纳瓦霍印第安人。

sentences.en: I know, I mean, they start just telling you a whole story about who they are and where they came from.
sentences.zh: 我知道，我的意思是，他们开始讲述关于他们是谁以及来自哪里的整个故事。

sentences.en: What is happening with these people?
sentences.zh: 这些人身上发生了什么？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, uh, one of the best researchers that I've ever met is Mike Nash and that, uh, a university of Tennessee.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我见过的最优秀的研究人员之一是田纳西大学的迈克·纳什（Mike Nash）。

sentences.en: And someone ran that question by me said, past life regression is fine.
sentences.zh: 有人问过我这个问题，他说，前世回溯没问题。

sentences.en: If you're looking at things from the standpoint of religion, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你是从宗教的角度来看待这些事情，对吧？

sentences.en: That's a religious phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 那是一种宗教现象。

sentences.en: Now, um, with, uh, if you hit one of the things that really happens with hypnosis is that people have very vivid imagery.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你……催眠中真正发生的事情之一是人们有非常生动的意象。

sentences.en: Remember the, the brain kind of shifts over and, and so things can be seen, become very real.
sentences.zh: 记住，大脑会发生某种转换，所以事物可以被看到，变得非常真实。

sentences.en: And, and that's why there was a huge, one of the most embarrassing periods of psychology is when people were planting suggestions for early
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么心理学最尴尬的时期之一是人们通过催眠植入早期创伤的暗示，而不是让病人自己回忆，而是植入那些暗示，催眠可以让虚假记忆看起来非常真实。

sentences.en: trauma through hypnosis and not letting the hypno, the patient arrived to him, but planning those and hypnosis can make a false memory appear very real.
sentences.zh: （接上句）催眠可以让虚假记忆看起来非常真实。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Uh, reminds me of Mike Nash had a patient that was, uh, reported he was abducted by aliens.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这让我想起迈克·纳什有一位病人，他声称自己被外星人绑架了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So he took him in hypnosis and they went through the whole abduction and came back and he didn't really question it, but he used it as a
sentences.zh: 所以他对他进行了催眠，他们经历了整个绑架过程，回来后他并没有真正质疑它，但他将其作为一种精神分析上的象征性事物，病人好多了，但他并没有真正质疑绑架是否真实。

sentences.en: symbolic thing for psychoanalytically and a patient got a lot better, but he didn't really question whether the abduction was real or not.
sentences.zh: （接上句）但他并没有真正质疑绑架是否真实。

sentences.en: Similarly, when you hypnotize you, if you give suggestions for past life regression with hypnosis, people, as you said, can have very vivid images.
sentences.zh: 同样，当你催眠时，如果你给出前世回溯的暗示，人们正如你所说，可以有非常生动的意象。

sentences.en: Now, I think it's very interesting that everyone seems to go back to the 17th century and, and be run over by a carriage.
sentences.zh: 现在，我觉得非常有趣的是，每个人似乎都回到了17世纪，被马车碾过。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Um, so my question, the way I say, uh, the way I see regression to past lives, if you hypnotize me, how far back am I going to go in human evolution?
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我的问题是，我看待前世回溯的方式是，如果你催眠我，我在人类进化史上能回溯到多远？

sentences.en: And I, I often say that if you hypnotize me, I'd probably go back to a newt, you know, and just, I would just be this wiggling thing because I, that's
sentences.zh: 我经常说，如果你催眠我，我可能会回到蝾螈的状态，你知道，我只会是那个扭动的东西，因为那是……

sentences.en: one of the things like when you really look at science and evolution, it's like, you know, uh, we didn't start in the 17th century or any time close to that.
sentences.zh: 当你真正审视科学和进化时，我们并不是从17世纪或任何接近那个时候开始的。

sentences.en: I'm remembering the primordial slime.
sentences.zh: 我正在回忆原始粘液。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But, but it is possible to take people back in their own lives.
sentences.zh: 但是，让人回到他们自己的一生中是可能的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that's legitimate.
sentences.zh: 那是合法的。

sentences.en: I mean, those are things that can be checked.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那些是可以核实的事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, uh, you know, it's one of the techniques, uh, one of the really powerful, powerful techniques of hypnosis
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是催眠真正强大的技术之一，

sentences.en: is that if someone's in pain or they're depressed, you can take them back earlier in life, uh, to happier times.
sentences.zh: 如果某人处于痛苦或抑郁中，你可以带他们回到生命中更早、更快乐的时光。

sentences.en: And you can really have them, uh, integrate those resources.
sentences.zh: 你可以让他们真正整合那些资源。

sentences.en: Uh, so, and then you bring them back to the present and they still have this, this really positive affect.
sentences.zh: 所以，然后你把他们带回现在，他们仍然拥有这种非常积极的情感。

sentences.en: I wanted to mention, speaking of past life regression, one of the, when I was in graduate school, I read a paper in journal of abnormal psychology that fascinated me.
sentences.zh: 我想提一下，说到前世回溯，我在研究生院时读过一篇《变态心理学杂志》上的论文，让我着迷。

sentences.en: And the study is they took adults and they gave them a computer task that you need eidetic imagery to do.
sentences.zh: 这项研究是他们找来成年人，给他们一项需要照相式记忆才能完成的电脑任务。

sentences.en: And there's a theory that we all have eidetic imagery before language as children.
sentences.zh: 有一种理论认为，我们在儿童时期掌握语言之前都拥有照相式记忆。

sentences.en: I don't know how accurate that is, but they regress these adults to children and they were able to do the task more.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这有多准确，但他们将这些成年人退行到儿童状态，他们确实能更好地完成任务。

sentences.en: Uh, and that was, I think one of the, the reasons I really got interested in hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想这就是我真正对催眠产生兴趣的原因之一。

sentences.en: And so I don't know if it was replicated, but I think just the concept was so creative and fascinating, but yes, we can, you can definitely
sentences.zh: 所以我不知道它是否被复现过，但我认为这个概念本身非常有创意且引人入胜，是的，我们确实可以，你绝对可以

sentences.en: regress people when you're regressing them.
sentences.zh: 在进行催眠回溯时引导人们。

sentences.en: You have to be really careful.
sentences.zh: 你必须非常小心。

sentences.en: If you just let them go anywhere, you can bring up some really damaging material that people can't really deal with.
sentences.zh: 如果你任由他们随意回溯，可能会引出一些极具破坏性的内容，而人们往往无法处理这些内容。

sentences.en: So when I'm using it clinically, I say, find yourself going back to early images in time, as long as they're positive images and as long as you feel safe.
sentences.zh: 所以当我在临床中使用它时，我会说，试着回到过去早期的影像中，只要那是积极的影像，只要你感到安全。

sentences.en: So, um, so yes, I hope that answers that.
sentences.zh: 所以，嗯，是的，希望这能回答你的问题。

sentences.en: You know, some of this sounds very similar to some of the psychedelic therapy that's happening right now, like a year and a half ago or something like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这听起来和目前正在进行的一些迷幻疗法非常相似，大概是一年半前左右吧。

sentences.en: I talked to somebody who's doing that kind of therapy and it's the same sort of thing that you, you need somebody guiding you
sentences.zh: 我和一位从事那种疗法的人聊过，情况是一样的，你需要有人引导你

sentences.en: through it, that you don't want to take people places that might be too dangerous.
sentences.zh: 经历整个过程，你不会想把人们带到可能过于危险的地方。

sentences.en: Is there something similar?
sentences.zh: 有什么相似之处吗？

sentences.en: Do you think that's happening with people who might be doing psychedelic therapy and doing hypnotherapy?
sentences.zh: 你认为那些同时进行迷幻疗法和催眠疗法的人身上也会发生这种情况吗？

sentences.en: Um, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，绝对会。

sentences.en: Uh, have to respond somewhat personally.
sentences.zh: 呃，我得从个人角度回应一下。

sentences.en: I lost a son over last year and, uh, I, uh, decided I'd been referring some of my terminal patients to psychedelic therapy, but I
sentences.zh: 去年我失去了一个儿子，呃，我，呃，决定我之前一直把一些绝症患者转介给迷幻疗法，但我

sentences.en: decided to pursue it myself in Denver with two top-notch therapists.
sentences.zh: 决定自己在丹佛找两位顶尖的治疗师亲自尝试一下。

sentences.en: And, uh, I did a psilocybin trip, uh, with again, with the two therapists, but I was amazed at how much similarity there is to the way I do advanced hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 而且，呃，我进行了一次裸盖菇素之旅，呃，同样是和那两位治疗师一起，但我惊讶地发现，这和我进行高级催眠的方式有如此多的相似之处。

sentences.en: And when the guide was introducing what would have, what was going to happen, it sounded very much like advanced hypnosis and it ended up being very useful for me.
sentences.zh: 当引导师介绍即将发生的事情时，听起来非常像高级催眠，最终对我来说也非常有帮助。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So last question.
sentences.zh: 最后一个问题。

sentences.en: I like to ask this often with people who are doing interesting work out there in the field.
sentences.zh: 我经常喜欢问那些在领域内做着有趣工作的人这个问题。

sentences.en: What are you working on now?
sentences.zh: 你现在在忙些什么？

sentences.en: What are the big questions you'd like to answer?
sentences.zh: 你想要解答的重大问题是什么？

sentences.en: What I'm working on now, I'm working on a second edition of my APA book, but the real focus is I'm
sentences.zh: 我现在正在做的是，我正在编写我的美国心理学会（APA）书籍的第二版，但真正的重点是

sentences.en: very interested in the neurophysiology of the way the mind works and the notion that basically
sentences.zh: 我对思维运作方式的神经生理学非常感兴趣，以及这样一个基本观点：

sentences.en: we think when we don't really have a self, we can only talk about what ourselves are not, but what we think is ourself is always a transient process, very Zen-like type of thing.
sentences.zh: 我们认为自己拥有一个“自我”，但实际上我们并没有，我们只能谈论我们“不是”什么，而我们所认为的“自我”始终是一个瞬时的过程，这非常有禅意。

sentences.en: But a lot of the way I think we get into trouble is by focusing on the past and the future, which are both illusions of the mind.
sentences.zh: 但我认为我们陷入困境的很大一部分原因，在于我们总是关注过去和未来，而这两者都是思维的幻觉。

sentences.en: So I, uh, I very often teach, uh, patients how to meditate, but then I use hypnosis to, again, I think the greatest use of hypnosis is just to, uh,
sentences.zh: 所以我，呃，我经常教，呃，患者如何冥想，但随后我会使用催眠，再次强调，我认为催眠最大的用途就是，呃，

sentences.en: accelerate psychotherapy, different learning process, but to have a good foundation.
sentences.zh: 加速心理治疗，这是一种不同的学习过程，但前提是要有良好的基础。

sentences.en: So I'm, uh, I, I'm particularly interested in now is, is, uh, uh, somewhat of a Buddhist understanding of the
sentences.zh: 所以我，呃，我，我现在特别感兴趣的是，呃，呃，某种程度上佛教对

sentences.en: mind as process rather than a fixed entity and getting away from dualistic thinking and explain that through science and then augment it through hypnosis.
sentences.zh: 思维作为一种过程而非固定实体的理解，并摆脱二元对立的思维，通过科学来解释这一点，再通过催眠来加强它。

sentences.en: That sounds amazing.
sentences.zh: 这听起来太棒了。

sentences.en: I look forward to seeing this as, as you work on, on the next edition of your book.
sentences.zh: 我很期待在你编写下一版书籍时看到这些内容。

sentences.en: So I want to thank you, Dr. Patterson for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 那么，我要感谢帕特森博士今天加入我的节目。

sentences.en: It's been really a lot of fun talking to you.
sentences.zh: 和你交谈真的非常愉快。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你，金。
